purpose: Acetohydroxamic acid is used to help treat a type of kidney stone called a struvite stone, which is caused by certain bacterial infections in the urinary tract. It is usually used along with antibiotics and sometimes other treatments. It helps stop the stones from growing bigger or coming back.
how_it_works: Some bacteria in your urinary tract produce an enzyme called urease, which makes your urine more alkaline and causes certain minerals to form stones. Acetohydroxamic acid works by blocking that enzyme so the bacteria cannot do as much damage. This helps keep your urine chemistry more normal and slows or stops stone formation.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include headache, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, feeling tired or weak, mild skin rash, hair thinning, and shakiness or trembling. Some people may also feel anxious or have mild mood changes.
warnings: This medication should NOT be taken during pregnancy because it can cause serious birth defects. You should use reliable birth control while taking it. It can also cause a type of anemia (low red blood cells), so your doctor will monitor your blood regularly. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine as it can cause a serious reaction including flushing and rash. People with kidney or liver problems may need special monitoring or may not be able to use this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, every 6 to 8 hours, for a total of about 10 to 15 mg per kilogram of body weight per day. It is taken by mouth with or without food. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on how your kidneys are working and how you respond to treatment.
